claims.object_text: encodes the sodium-activated potassium channel KNa1.1; preferential expression in frontal cortex, hippocampus, cerebellum, and brainstem
claims.quote: KCNT1 encodes the sodium-activated potassium channel KNa1.1, expressed preferentially in the frontal cortex, hippocampus, cerebellum, and brainstem.

claims.object_text: epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS); sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (SHE)
claims.quote: Pathogenic missense variants in KCNT1 are associated with intractable epilepsy, namely epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS), and sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (SHE).
In vitro studies of pathogenic KCNT1 variants support predominantly a gain-of-function molecular mechanism

claims.object_text: CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in mouse with a gain-of-function variant in endogenous Kcnt1 (heterozygous and homozygous)
claims.quote: Using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, we introduced a gain-of-function variant into the endogenous mouse Kcnt1 gene.

claims.object_text: heterozygous and homozygous knock-in mice displayed greater seizure susceptibility to kainate and pentylenetetrazole (PTZ) but not to flurothyl
claims.quote: Compared to wild-type (WT) littermates, heterozygous and homozygous knock-in mice displayed greater seizure susceptibility to the chemoconvulsants kainate and pentylenetetrazole (PTZ), but not to flurothyl.

claims.object_text: greater amplitude of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents in CA1 pyramidal neurons; greater inhibitory tone
claims.quote: CA1 hippocampal pyramidal neurons exhibit greater amplitude of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents in mutant mice with no difference in frequency, suggesting greater inhibitory tone associated with the Kcnt1 mutation.

claims.object_text: parvalbumin-expressing (PV+) interneurons fail to fire repetitively and are more prone to depolarization block
claims.quote: parvalbumin-expressing (PV+) interneurons failed to fire repetitively with large amplitude current injections and were more prone to depolarization block.

These alterations in firing can be recapitulated by direct application of the KNa1.1 channel activator loxapine in WT but are occluded in knock-in littermates, supporting a direct channel gain-of-function mechanism.

claims.object_text: KNa1.1 gain-of-function dampens interneuron excitability to a greater extent than it impacts pyramidal neuron excitability, driving seizure susceptibility
claims.quote: Taken together, these results suggest that KNa1.1 gain-of-function dampens interneuron excitability to a greater extent than it impacts pyramidal neuron excitability, driving seizure susceptibility in a mouse model of KCNT1-associated epilepsy.
